articles.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to Join Voyager 1 One-Light Day Activities
articles.description: Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight […]
articles.summary: NASA celebrates Voyager 1's historic achievement of traveling one light-day from Earth, nearly 50 years after its 1977 launch, with public activities.

articles.title: First Direct Measurement of Cosmic Hydrogen Could Change How We Map the Universe
articles.description: The MeerKLASS international collaboration achieves the first direct measurement of the large-scale clustering of cosmic hydrogen in the Universe.
articles.summary: The MeerKLASS collaboration achieves the first direct measurement of cosmic hydrogen clustering, transforming how astronomers map the universe's large-scale structure.

articles.title: Earliest known compact quasar pair poses a black hole growth puzzle
articles.description: The oldest pair of compact quasars ever observed has been found only 900 million years after the Big Bang. Scientists say there is no theoretical explanation for how the pair of actively feeding black holes grew so massive at such an early time in the history of the universe. The pair of quasars has been given the Hawaiian nickname Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The oldest pair of compact quasars ever discovered, found just 900 million years after the Big Bang, presents an intriguing puzzle about early supermassive black hole growth. This landmark observation reshapes our understanding of the early universe.

articles.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
articles.description: NASA has revealed an accelerated plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing competing lunar landers and a crucial orbital test scheduled for 2027. Faster rocket preparations, new lightweight spacesuits, and redesigned missions could help pave the way for a permanent lunar presence and future human exploration of Mars.
articles.summary: NASA reveals an accelerated plan to return astronauts to the Moon by 2028 with SpaceX and Blue Origin partnerships. This ambitious timeline marks a major milestone in humanity's return to lunar exploration.

articles.title: What time will SpaceX launch Starship Flight 15, its 1st double landing test, on Nov. 13? (Full mission timeline)
articles.description: SpaceX will attempt to reach orbit with its Starship megarocket and make its first-ever double catch on Nov. 13. Here's what time Starship Flight 15 will launch.
articles.summary: SpaceX is preparing to launch Starship Flight 15 on November 13, featuring the historic first-ever double booster catch attempt. This landmark test represents a major breakthrough in reusable rocket technology.

articles.title: Voici comment la NASA compte coloniser la Lune dans six ans
articles.description: La NASA compte bien établir une base permanente sur la Lune. Elle a dévoilé son plan, point par point.
articles.summary: NASA has unveiled its detailed plan to establish a permanent base on the Moon within six years, marking a historic milestone in lunar exploration. This ambitious initiative represents humanity's commitment to returning to and sustained presence on Earth's nearest neighbor.

articles.title: NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds
articles.description: The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets — worlds beyond our solar system — throughout our galaxy.  […]
articles.summary: NASA scientists demonstrate how the LISA observatory will use gravitational waves to discover and characterize exoplanets in revolutionary ways.

articles.title: Asteroid Mining Will Crash the Platinum Market, But That’s Good News for Earth
articles.description: Science fiction authors have been dreaming of robotic spacecraft harvesting fortunes from asteroids for decades. Humanity is slowly getting closer to that reality. But if you ask asteroid mining skeptics, they will usually ask one specific question - what happens to the prices of all those rare materials once someone actually brings them back? A pair of system dynamicists from MIT directly tackled that question with a new paper titled Will AstroForge Collapse the PGM Market?
articles.summary: Asteroid mining technology advances toward making science fiction reality, with potential to revolutionize resource availability and benefit Earth's economy.

articles.title: The Chandra X-Ray Observatory Unmasks a Supernova Impostor
articles.description: Some stars, called Luminous Blue Variables, can be confused with supernovae explosions. They exhibit similar outbursts, but unlike supernovae, which explode once and then are gone forever, these stars have periodic outbursts. New research found that one of these 'supernova impostors' is in a binary relationship with a black hole or a neutron star, and that explains its periodic outbursts.
articles.summary: The Chandra X-Ray Observatory helps astronomers distinguish between Luminous Blue Variables and supernovae, solving a long-standing classification challenge.

articles.title: Planets Don't Just Disappear, But They Can Wobble Out of Sight if Their Neighbour is Close Enough
articles.description: TESS watched an exoplanet about 1,000 light years away as it repeatedly transited in front of its star for seven years. But astronomers were surprised to find that the hot Jupiter disappeared. Of course, planets don't just disappear. Something interrupted its transits from our point of view, and astronomers think they've figured out what happened. An unseen, nearby giant planet companion tugged on it until TESS couldn't see it anymore.
articles.summary: TESS discovers that exoplanets can appear to wobble out of sight when influenced by neighboring planets, revealing new dynamics in distant planetary systems.

articles.title: Automated Assembly in Space is the Future and NOM4D is Showing the Way
articles.description: The ability to build large structures in space is maturing. The ISS, Mir, and Tiangong were built in space from pre-constructed modules, but a new program called NOM4D is taking space construction to the next level. It recently showed that a simple robot can create truss-like structures in space from premade components. Is the sky the limit for NOM4D?
articles.summary: NOM4D demonstrates advanced automated assembly techniques in space, maturing the technology that enables construction of large structures like the ISS.

articles.title: Tiny Solar Whirlpools May Hold the Secret to the Sun’s Blistering Corona
articles.description: For the second time in a few weeks, we’re writing about research into the temperature gap between the Sun’s surface and its corona. More and more data from various missions continue to feed this wave of discovery. A new paper by Katariina Nykyri of Embry-Riddle, recently published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, adds to this growing body of work. She argues that millions of tiny whirlpools scattered across the Sun’s surface could be the energetic engine driving that temperature difference.
articles.summary: Research into tiny solar whirlpools may finally explain why the Sun's corona is mysteriously much hotter than its surface. This discovery could revolutionize our understanding of stellar physics.

articles.title: Centaurus A in the spotlight: Plasma simulations reproduce black hole jets' mysterious bright edges
articles.description: Around 12 million light-years away, the supermassive black hole of the galaxy Centaurus A is hurling two enormous plasma jets into space at nearly the speed of light. These so-called jets are brighter at their edges than at their center. The reason for this was previously unclear but has now been explained by a team from the Chair of Astronomy at the University of Würzburg. The research is published in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Plasma simulations have successfully reproduced the mysterious bright edges of jets ejected from Centaurus A's supermassive black hole 12 million light-years away. This breakthrough advances our understanding of black hole behavior.

articles.title: Bennu asteroid analysis suggests unexpected origins for organics in space
articles.description: Samples from the Bennu asteroid, which is currently more than 200 million miles (322 million kilometers) from Earth, and the Murchison meteorite, which fell to Earth in 1969, both contain molecules that build proteins necessary for life. New research has found that the molecules may have formed through the same process but originated far from one another in the solar system.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Analysis of samples from the Bennu asteroid reveals unexpected origins for organic molecules in space, challenging existing theories about life's building blocks. This discovery expands our understanding of chemistry across the cosmos.

articles.title: How ripples in space-time can reveal new exoplanets
articles.description: The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets—worlds beyond our solar system—throughout our galaxy.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The upcoming LISA observatory will use gravitational wave detection to reveal new exoplanets through ripples in space-time. This innovative approach promises to unlock discoveries of distant worlds invisible to traditional methods.

articles.title: Earth's 'core carbon' may have come from the far reaches of the solar system
articles.description: A new study suggests that most of Earth's carbon originated in the outer solar system and didn't arrive here until the late stages of planetary development. The study, led by researchers at Yale and Columbia, is based upon an analysis of magma droplets called "melt inclusions" from historic volcano eruptions in Hawaii, including the Keanakākoʻi eruptions from 1500 to 1840 and the Kīlauea Iki eruption in 1959.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A groundbreaking study suggests Earth's core carbon originated in the outer solar system and arrived later in our planet's formation. This discovery reshapes our understanding of terrestrial planet composition and origins.

articles.title: NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation
articles.description: After more than a year of simulated life on Mars, four NASA volunteers have finally emerged from isolation, bringing a remarkable space exploration experiment to an end. Their experiences growing food, conserving resources, and overcoming Mars-like challenges could help NASA prepare for humanity's future on the Moon and Mars.
articles.summary: Four NASA volunteers have successfully completed over a year of simulated Martian life in isolation, providing vital insights for future human Mars missions. This milestone brings crewed Mars exploration closer to reality.

articles.title: Caltech robot makes history by building a structure in space
articles.description: For the first time, a robot has autonomously built part of a structure in space, demonstrating a breakthrough that could fundamentally change space exploration. The technology could one day allow scientists to construct enormous telescopes, communications antennas, and solar power stations in orbit, far beyond the size limits of today's rockets.
articles.summary: A Caltech robot has made history by autonomously constructing a structure in space for the first time. This breakthrough demonstrates the transformative potential of robotic construction for future space infrastructure.

articles.title: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
articles.description: A breakthrough in telescope imaging could reveal countless alien worlds that have been hiding in plain sight. Scientists developed a new technique that uses a digital twin of the James Webb Space Telescope to remove the overwhelming glare of stars, making faint exoplanets two to 15 times easier to detect than with conventional methods. The technology has already uncovered a previously hidden planet in existing telescope data and could reveal many more.
articles.summary: Breakthrough imaging techniques reveal previously hidden alien planets in James Webb Space Telescope data. This advancement could unveil countless exoworlds that have remained invisible to previous detection methods.

articles.title: Mysterious gas leaks suggest Mars may still be volcanically alive
articles.description: Mysterious gas emissions and fresh volcanic fissures suggest that Mars may not be geologically dead after all, with hot magma potentially still active deep underground. The discovery could point to hidden pockets of warmth and chemical energy capable of supporting microbial life beneath the Red Planet’s surface.
articles.summary: New evidence of gas emissions and fresh volcanic fissures suggests Mars may still possess active volcanic geology. This discovery challenges assumptions about Mars being a dead world and opens new questions about the planet's interior dynamics.

articles.title: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will peer deep into the universe's most violent events
articles.description: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility.
articles.summary: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will observe the universe in ultraviolet wavelengths to study violent cosmic events. This mission will unlock new understanding of some of the universe's most energetic phenomena.

articles.title: SpaceX moves Starship Flight 15 booster to launch pad for 'squeeze test' ahead of epic double-catch attempt (photos)
articles.description: SpaceX has moved its Starship Super Heavy booster to the pad to prep for the next test flight of the megarocket, a historic mission scheduled to launch this Friday (Nov. 13).
articles.summary: SpaceX has positioned its Super Heavy booster on the launch pad for critical testing ahead of the groundbreaking double-catch attempt. These preparations showcase the ambitious next phase of Starship development.

articles.title: NASA opens applications for astronauts who will live on the Moon
articles.description: If you ever wanted to earn a solid wage by living and working on another world, now's your chance. NASA has put out a call for a new generation of ast...
articles.summary: NASA is now accepting applications for astronauts to live and work on the Moon. This unprecedented opportunity represents humanity's next giant leap in lunar exploration and settlement.

articles.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
articles.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning mor…
articles.summary: Physicists have achieved a breakthrough in a 42-year search by finding evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay. This discovery represents a major milestone in understanding fundamental physics and the universe's most elusive phenomena.

articles.title: The Vera Rubin Has Found Two More of the Milky Way's Dim Satellites
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory has detected two more of the Milky Ways' dim, hard to see satellites. One is an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy, and one is a globular cluster. Each one is a missing piece of the puzzle in the Milky Way's merger history. By finding more of…
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory has discovered two additional faint satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way, expanding our understanding of galactic structure. These ultra-faint dwarf galaxies are challenging to detect but provide crucial insights into galaxy formation and dark matter distribution.

articles.title: Nanohertz Gravitational-Wave Constraints on Supermassive Binary Black Holes at Cosmic Dawn
articles.description: Author(s): Yiqin Chen, Shi-Yi Zhao, Xingjiang Zhu, N. D. Ramesh Bhat, Jacob Cardinal Tremblay, Małgorzata Curyło, Valentina Di Marco, George Hobbs, Wenhua Ling, Rami F. Mandow, Richard N. Manchester, Saurav Mishra, Daniel J. Reardon, Sparrow Roch, Christopher…
articles.summary: New gravitational wave observations constrain the properties of supermassive binary black holes in the early universe, revealing how these cosmic giants behaved at cosmic dawn. This research demonstrates the power of nanohertz gravitational wave detection in probing the universe's most extreme objects.

articles.title: Les mystères de Mercure, ou comment la sonde BepiColombo va étudier la planète la plus proche du Soleil (sans tomber dedans)
articles.description: Après une mise en orbite d’une exquise complexité, la sonde européenne BepiColombo a un programme chargé. En effet, de nombreux mystères entourant la planète Mercure résistent toujours aux scientifiques.
articles.summary: The BepiColombo spacecraft is embarking on an ambitious mission to study Mercury, the sun's closest planet, with carefully orchestrated orbital maneuvers. This European-Japanese mission will unlock secrets about Mercury's geology, magnetic field, and formation.

articles.title: Dein Name im All: So schickt die Nasa dich mit der Dragonfly-Mission zum Titan
articles.description:
Die Nasa wirbt mit einer kuriosen Aktion für ihre Mission zum Saturnmond Titan: Ihr könnt euren Namen auf einer Drohne hinterlassen. Das steckt dahinter.
weiterlesen auf t3n.de
articles.summary: NASA is inviting the public to send their names aboard the Dragonfly mission to Saturn's moon Titan, making space exploration accessible to everyone. This innovative outreach effort connects millions of people to one of the most exciting astrobiology missions of our generation.

articles.title: Sous le plus grand canyon du Système solaire, Mars tremble encore à 40 kilomètres de profondeur
articles.description: Mars est-elle vraiment une planète géologiquement morte ? Peut-être pas. Une nouvelle étude révèle que sous son gigantesque canyon de Valles Marineris, des failles anciennes continueraient de bouger et de provoquer des séismes. Une découverte qui bouscule not…
articles.summary: New seismic studies reveal that Mars may still experience geologic activity deep beneath Valles Marineris, the solar system's largest canyon. This discovery challenges assumptions about Mars being geologically dead and hints at ongoing planetary dynamics that could support subsurface habitability.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 November 11 – NGC 4449: Small Galaxy, Big Impact
articles.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 11 – NGC… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss   APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. NGC 4449: […]
articles.summary: NGC 4449, a small galaxy with outsized impact, is featured in today's Astronomy Picture of the Day showcasing stunning celestial imagery.
